Objective: Identify early behavioural engagement patterns associated with at-risk outcomes.
Evidence: OULAD and KDD analyses showed consistently higher early engagement among lower-risk outcome groups.
Key_Result: All four aligned engagement features showed consistent direction across both cohorts.

Objective: Develop predictive models using early engagement features.
Evidence: Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost were evaluated using leakage-safe stratified cross-validation.
Key_Result: OULAD XGBoost AU-ROC = 0.7971; KDD XGBoost AU-ROC = 0.8542.

Objective: Provide interpretable evidence about which behavioural features contribute to predictions.
Evidence: Native XGBoost feature contributions were analysed.
Key_Result: Active days, total interactions and unique resources were among the largest contributors.

Objective: Assess whether predictive patterns remain consistent across different learning cohorts.
Evidence: Cross-cohort feature alignment, effect sizes, direction consistency and bidirectional model transfer were evaluated.
Key_Result: All four aligned features showed 100% directional consistency; bidirectional transfer produced AU-ROC values of 0.7795 and 0.7470.

Objective: Examine fairness-related differences in predictive behaviour.
Evidence: Prediction performance was examined across gender, age and disability groups in OULAD.
Key_Result: TPR and FPR varied across groups, indicating the importance of subgroup evaluation rather than relying only on overall accuracy.
